=== page_019.jpg ===
xvii
PREFACE.
43 SIDNEY STREET,
CAMBRIDGE.
The Publisher has pleasure in issuing the 1931-32 edition
of Spalding's Street and General Directory of Cambridge, which
is the thirty-first volume of the work, the first one of which
was issued in 1874.
The number of houses in the Borough continues to show
an appreciable increase, which has taken place during the past
year chiefly in Glebe Road, Holbroke Road, Leys Avenue,
Milton Road, Mowbray Road, Orchard Avenue, and Sedley
Taylor Road, while the following new thoroughfares have
been opened: Ascham Road, Barrow Road, Kendal Way,
Linden Close, and Shirley Grove. A large estate is also in course of
preparation between Histon Road and Milton Road, where a
new thoroughfare named Gilbert Road will run.
Numbering or renumbering has taken place since the last
edition of the Directory was issued in Castle Street, Cavendish
Road, Flamsteed Road, Glebe Road, Holbroke Road, King's
Hedges Road, Latham Road, Leys Avenue, Orchard Avenue,
S. Andrew's Road, and York Terrace.
The disappearance of the formerly familiar Carrier's Cart
is shown by the Villages section, where it will be seen that this
work is now done aimost entirely by Motor transport.
The Publisher again tenders his thanks to those who have
readily supplied information for the Directory, and to the
Subscribers and Advertisers, and trusts the book will prove of
much benefit to them.
W. P. SPALDING,
Publisher.
September, 1931.

xxxvi. CAMBRIDGE DIRECTORY-OFFICIAL INFORMATION.
BURIAL GROUNDS IN CAMBRIDGE.
The Borough Cemetery, Newmarket Road.— The area of the Cemetery is 25a. 21. 32p.
and it is 2} miles distant from Great S. Mary's Church in an easterly direction. It
adjoins the main road between Cambridge and Newmarket. The soil is gravel and
chalk marl, the level being 50 ft. above Ordnance datum, or about 36 ft. above the
river Cam. The land is drained to a depth of io ft. by means of agricultural pipes.
There are 22,000 grave spaces, and room is left for a Crematorium. The buildings
erected include the Superintendent's Residence, Shelter, Waiting Room, &c. There
is no consecrated Chapel upon the ground (which is not to be consecrated as a whole
by the Bishop), but there is a room in which a part of any Burial Service may be said.
HOURS FOR BURIALS.
From October to March (inclusive), between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
" April to September "  " ga.m. and 5 p.m.
No morning interments on Sundays. Special arrangements may be made.

and Bank Holidays excepted).
